newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel halts peace talks with Palestinians.
newsitem.headline: Israel halts peace talks with Palestinians.

text.p: Israel is halting peace talks with the Palestinians following a suicide bombing that killed 15 people in Jerusalem, a government spokesman said on Wednesday.

Asked if negotiations would resume as announced earlier this week, spokesman Shai Bazak told Israel Radio: "No, for the moment the ministerial committee has determined that in order for it to be possible to make progress in the process, the Palestinian Authority must first of all carry out its commitments to fight terrorism."

"At this stage no steps will be taken so long as the Palestinian Authority doesn't take steps it committed to," Bazak said after a meeting of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's ministerial committee on national security.

Netanyahu has accused Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat of failing to do enough to halt the attacks of Moslem militants. A leaflet claimed responsibility for Wednesday's attack at a Jerusalem market in the name of the Moslem militant Hamas movement.

Israel and the Palestinians agreed earlier this week to resume negotiations on carrying out interim peace accords already signed on such issues as a Gaza airport and seaport and safe passage for Palestinians between the West Bank and Gaza.

"The ministerial committee on national security sees the Palestinian Authority as responsible for acts of terrorism and for the murder of innocent civilians in Jerusalem in that it didn't take the steps that it was obligated to take, among them the war against terrorist organisations and their infrastructure," Bazak said.
